Machine Learning in Production

Artificial intelligence and machine learning have transformed how we build software. Deep learning models are now deployed in production systems at scale.

This article explores the challenges of deploying neural networks, including model serving, monitoring, and continuous training pipelines.

The best model is the one that ships.

Infrastructure

Modern ML infrastructure requires careful consideration of compute resources, data pipelines, and model versioning. Teams use frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch for training, then convert to optimized formats for serving.

Kubernetes has become the standard platform for orchestrating model serving containers, with tools like Seldon and KServe providing ML-specific abstractions.

  • Model registry for versioning
  • Feature store for data consistency
  • A/B testing for model comparison

Monitoring

Production ML systems require monitoring beyond standard application metrics. Teams must track model drift, data quality, and prediction distributions to catch degradation early.

Alerting on prediction confidence scores helps identify when models encounter out-of-distribution inputs that may produce unreliable results.

Organizations that invest in observability for their ML systems see faster iteration cycles and fewer production incidents related to model quality.
